body: whole-file-ownership-records-omit-doc-and-test-sprints: Evidence, re-verified: decision:whole-file-ownership's Records paragraph says true-up 'moves them and never rewrites their bodies, save a live sprint's retired boilerplate (see also: live-sprints-brought-current-on-true-up)'. decision:live-sprints-brought-current-on-true-up, amended by the sixth intake drain sprint, says 'True-up brings each sprint, documentation sprint, and test sprint not yet archived to the structure and boilerplate the carried release reads' and, for a documentation or test sprint, 'brings the plan's shape current, such as filling a field the carried tools require from the project's configuration'. concept:sprint says a documentation sprint 'is not a sprint in this sense', and a test sprint 'is not one either', so 'a live sprint' in whole-file-ownership excludes both, and the two decisions contradict each other. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: the sixth intake drain sprint amended live-sprints and left whole-file-ownership's sentence as it stood; a reader of whole-file-ownership alone concludes true-up never touches a documentation or test sprint. Corpus change: whole-file-ownership's Records paragraph stops contradicting the later ruling in live-sprints-brought-current-on-true-up; the rule that forces it is that the corpus contradicting a later ruling yields to it (the route's own rule), and design docs describe the project as it stands. Two wordings comply, and they differ only in form: A names both exceptions in the paragraph (a sprint's retired boilerplate and a documentation or test sprint's plan shape, each not yet archived), matching the paragraph's current inline-exception-plus-see-also form; B names no exception and defers wholly to live-sprints-brought-current-on-true-up, which says each fact once. Recommend A: it keeps the paragraph's existing form and a reader of whole-file-ownership alone learns every exception; flip to B if the owner prefers the exception stated in one place only. Harm: corpus wording only; no accept-list entry. Siblings: none.

second-recorded-test-run-refuses-or-waits: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:round_lock (L2041-L2049) takes fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) on .ok-planner/.cache/tests-<sprint>.lock and, on BlockingIOError, raises InputError 'another recorded run of <sprint> is under way and writes <sprint>-results.jsonl: wait for it to end, then run again'; tests:cmd_run (L2143-L2148) holds that lock for the whole round whenever the run is recorded (--sprint given, no --from, no --only). The filed problem holds. Mechanism: a recorded run appends a header, one line per result, and a closing line to the sprint's -results.jsonl; two at once used to interleave into a round no complete run produced (A1), and the lock ends that either way. Corpus: no concept or decision decides what a second recorded run does; decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests, decision:tests-isolated-unless-declared and decision:scenario-list-decided-once are silent on concurrent recorded runs. The tests tool is the project's own shipped script (.ok-planner/review/project.md lists it), so A3 governs its user-facing behavior: 'two sessions at once' counts as a user's mistake, and a stall or an error that does not tell the user what they did wrong is the harm. Options: A refuse at once, naming the run under way and telling the user to wait (built now; cost: a second session must retry by hand). B block until the first run ends, then run its own round (cost: a session stalls silently for a whole suite run, which A3 names as a stall unless the user sees why; two queued rounds run back to back with no retry logic). C (filer missed) wait, but print one line naming the run under way before it blocks, with the wait bounded by a configuration key (cost: a new setting, which decision:settings-have-no-code-defaults requires true-up to write into every project, and a time-out branch that still refuses). Recommend A: it tells the user exactly what is happening, adds no setting, and no test sprint run needs two recorded rounds at once; flip to C if the owner expects sessions to queue rounds unattended. Siblings: none.

doc-edit-rules-ignore-docspec-notes: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/core.md:DOC-EDIT-RULES (L7-L28) lists seven rules (false claim; missing listed element; internal element listed; closed sprint not reflected; departs from ## Shape or ## Where layout; departs from ## Reader or ## Covers; unsettleable claim) and ends 'Every other sentence stays as written.' No rule names ## Notes. The writer's prompt (core.md:DOC-WRITE-PROMPT, L211-L214) reads Notes, so a file written whole honors it. The docspec definition (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md L176) says Notes 'carries the owner's standing instructions to the writer: an outline, a passage to keep verbatim, a thing to leave out'. The filed problem holds. Mechanism: when the owner adds or changes a Notes instruction while files exist, bin/docs window opens the docspec, the planner finds no rule that fires on any file, the docspec gets no item, and its stamp moves past the instruction. Corpus: decision:documentation-edits-only-where-a-rule-fires states the same fixed rule set the code carries ('Every other sentence stays as written') and its rationale names why reader and coverage got a rule ('without the rule, documentation never follows the owner's change to whom it is for or what it covers'); it is silent on Notes. story:declare-project-documentation promises 'whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'. So a code-only fix would break the decision's fixed set: the fix changes what the corpus commits to, and the owner chooses. Harm: A3 via the drive failure on story declare-project-documentation, confirmed by a merge agent in sprint certification of the sixth intake drain sprint. Options: A add an edit rule, in the decision and in DOC-EDIT-RULES, that fires where a file departs from its docspec's ## Notes, and the writer rewrites the passage that departs (cost: another judgment-based rule, so a run that meets a changed Notes rewrites more prose). B keep the fixed set, and amend the decision to say Notes bind only files written whole, with a changed Notes reaching existing files only when the owner asks a documentation sprint to rewrite them (cost: the story's promise narrows; the owner's new instruction never reaches existing files on its own). C have a change to a docspec's Notes since its stamp mark every file it governs for a whole rewrite (cost: churn of text no Notes instruction touches, which the decision's alternatives reject). Recommend A: it is the same move the decision already made for Reader and Covers, for the same reason; flip to B if the owner wants documentation runs to churn as little as possible. Siblings: doc-style-pass-may-undo-docspec-notes (routed defect this run: the style pass gets the limit to keep what Notes orders); rule them in one sprint so the writer and the style pass both honor Notes.
